requirements.requirement: | P1 | **Full parity** | Every capability a user can reach through the GUI (menu item, toolbar button, tool gesture, dialog field, context-menu entry, keyboard shortcut, drag-and-drop, panel action, preference) MUST be reachable through a registered command. Everything a user can *see* (document content, current state, rendered output, warnings) MUST be readable through queries, resources or renders. A GUI feature without a command is a defect. |
requirements.note: Builder: GUI parity/gestures M4, render and scene determinism M3; kernel determinism already tested. Explicit implementing owner checkpoints: builder M3 C3.3, M4 C4.2.

requirements.requirement: | P2 | **One command layer** | The GUI and the MCP server are both clients of the same command registry and document model. The GUI MUST NOT mutate the document by any path that bypasses the registry. This is what guarantees P1. |
requirements.note: Within the implemented M1 kernel; domain operations keep their declared later owners.

requirements.requirement: | P3 | **Structured first, gestural second** | Every gestural operation (drawing, painting, dragging, transforming) MUST have a structured equivalent that takes explicit data (points, ids, numbers). Raw input simulation (§7.6) also exists for tool-faithful reproduction and UI testing, but no task SHOULD require it. |
requirements.note: Builder: GUI parity/gestures M4, render and scene determinism M3; kernel determinism already tested. Explicit implementing owner checkpoints: builder M3 C3.3, M4 C4.2.

requirements.requirement: | P4 | **Explicit targets** | Commands that act on "the current selection / current element / current frame" in the GUI MUST also accept explicit target parameters. When targets are omitted the current UI context is used, and the result MUST report what was actually targeted. |
requirements.note: Within the implemented M1 kernel; domain operations keep their declared later owners.

requirements.requirement: | P5 | **Never block** | No command invoked by an agent may open a modal dialog, file picker, colour picker or confirmation box, or wait for user input. Choices become parameters; confirmations become a structured protocol (§6.3). |
requirements.note: Round-one fix verified on 39ea1b2; proving tests listed.

requirements.requirement: | P6 | **Verifiable** | After any change an agent MUST be able to verify the outcome: each mutating call returns the list of changed objects and their new revisions; queries return complete JSON; renders return images; `describe_frame` returns a structured description of what is visible. |
requirements.note: Builder: GUI parity/gestures M4, render and scene determinism M3; kernel determinism already tested. Explicit implementing owner checkpoints: builder M3 C3.3, M4 C4.2.

requirements.requirement: | P7 | **Deterministic** | Given the same document and the same command sequence, the resulting document and rendered pixels MUST be identical. Randomness (particles, jitter, auto-naming) MUST be seeded and recorded in the document. |
requirements.note: Builder: GUI parity/gestures M4, render and scene determinism M3; kernel determinism already tested. Explicit implementing owner checkpoints: builder M3 C3.3, M4 C4.2.

requirements.requirement: | P8 | **Safe and attributable** | Agent sessions run under explicit permission scopes. Destructive, file-overwriting and outward-facing (network) actions require confirmation according to policy. Every agent action is logged, attributed in undo history, and can be undone. The user can pause or disconnect an agent at any time. |
requirements.note: C14-R3-01 commit accounting closes, and atomic revisions/history replay passes; C14-R3-02 remains divergent: group expectRev is rejected as an unknown field. Owner builder C1.4 before M1 merge.

requirements.requirement: | P9 | **Discoverable and economical** | An agent with no prior knowledge MUST be able to discover all commands, their schemas, examples and the object model from the server itself. Responses MUST be compact by default (projections, pagination, summaries), because agents work with limited context. |

requirements.requirement: - **Command registry.** Each command declares: `id`, `kind` (`action`, `toggle`, `query`, `job`, `ui`, `event`), human label and description, parameter JSON Schema, result JSON Schema, enablement rule (with a human-readable reason when disabled), undo label, permission scope(s) (§6.1), whether confirmation may be required, and at least one example invocation. Registration happens at startup; plug-ins MAY register further commands under their own namespace.
requirements.note: Within the implemented M1 kernel; domain operations keep their declared later owners.

requirements.requirement: - **GUI binding.** Menus, toolbars, context menus, shortcuts and dialogs are bound to command ids. A dialog collects parameters and invokes the command once on OK; a tool gesture builds the parameter set of a structured command (e.g. a brush gesture produces a `draw.stroke.add` call with the sampled points and pressures). This binding is what makes P1 testable (§14).

requirements.requirement: - **Executor.** All document mutations from all clients go through one serialized queue on the document thread. GUI input and agent calls are interleaved at command granularity; a command or batch is never interleaved with another mutation.
